newsitem.title: USA: Arizona Navajo coal-fired unit back up to 725 MW.
newsitem.headline: Arizona Navajo coal-fired unit back up to 725 MW.

text.p: The 755 megawatt (MW) unit 1 at the Navajo coal-fired power plant in Page, Ariz., was operating at 725 MW as of early Monday, sources familiar with the plant's operations said.
They noted that the unit's operating capacity has been raised from around 720 MW due to upgrades made during the recent maintenance shutdown that began November 9.
Unit 1 is expected to remain curtailed by about 30 MW for economic reasons, the sources noted.
Navajo's 750 MW unit 2 and 750 MW unit 3 are also curtailed, by 85 MW and 100 MW, respectively, for the same reason, they said.

The Navajo unit is operated by the Phoenix-based Salt River Project, which also holds a 21.7-percent equity stake in the plant. Other owners include the U.S. Bureau of Reclamation (24.3 percent), Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (21.2 percent), Arizona Public Service Co (14 percent), Nevada Power (11.3 percent) and Tucson Electric Power (7.5 percent).
